method.field: The same 36 distinct real activity clips as the earlier motion panel; all source hashes verified in that panel. A frame cue is a mean absolute difference of at least 18 on a 0..255 scale. Base: reduce luminance to 64x36 before differencing. Experimental additional cue: mean over absolute RGB pixel differences at normal contact-sheet resolution. Adjacent cue frames can belong to the same ongoing movement. Compute both on the first eight seconds; apply the ordinary two-second maximum and half-second minimum pause rules. Verify those clocks against all sixteen blind online session receipts.
method.online: Choose eight by SHA-256 of reel-picture-difference-01/ plus the clip ID, without event or cue selection. Real Reel MCP view, max_seconds=2, picture only, no audio, until=8. One fresh local signed-in Codex gpt-6.1-terra per arm and clip, no shell, plugins, filename clue or answer key. Submit marks before the next interval is released. Compare marks in [0.3,8) with each of five human observers on the full source. One-to-one F1 with 0.5 s tolerance, equal weight per viewer then film; 10000 paired bootstrap draws over films. The archive does not establish human audio settings. The interval does not measure repeated-model variability. The experimental RGB pause rule was not adopted.
method.online_prompt: Watch the activity as it unfolds. Mark the times when one meaningful part of the main activity ends and another begins, one level below the overall activity. Include a change of shot. An ongoing activity may continue across many pictures. It is fine to mark several changes in an interval or none. Use advance with consecutive turn numbers starting at 1. At each call submit your changes in the preceding interval in seconds from the start of the film. Finish when the server returns end_of_view.
method.control: Silent 320x180 RGB FFV1 at 20 fps for four seconds. A brief excursion lasts 3 frames starting at interval + .3 s, ending at interval + .45 s. Hue: [220,20,20] and [20,122,20] both map to integer luma 80. Pattern: grey values [40,40,110,180,180] tile horizontally, shifted by two columns. Light: base red to [198,198,198]. Steady: same every frame. Changes cover the full frame on even case indices and the central half of the rows on odd indices. Source hashes identify the generated recordings.
method.lane: Each signed-in local Codex session sees only the time ruler and change row cropped from the product page at native pixel scale. Baseline crops verified byte-for-byte (pixels) using a separate copy of the old code. Readers have no source frames or audio on this task. An exact hit is the complete set of one-second bins, including an empty set on a steady film.
method.lane_prompt: Read the time ruler and picture-change row from a four-second recording (0 to 4 s; the short tick marks are 1, 2, 3 s). White spikes show changes between consecutively displayed pictures. The red line marks a held picture and the yellow line shows brightness. In which one-second intervals was there visible change? Choose zero or more interval start times from 0,1,2,3. Return only {"intervals":[...]}.
method.direct: Separate direct stdio MCP full_detail=true with images and timed RGB measurements, signed-in local Codex; no answer key or shell. One read on each of eight controls, one constant-looking duplicate-PTS recording and one prefix ending at the first change. The duplicate-PTS source contains luminance levels [42,220,42,42] at microseconds [0,100000,100000,300000]. Last picture at each timestamp is visible. Field delivery hashes cover all compact text and image blocks through end-of-view; the filename and local paths were not passed to GPT.
method.direct_prompt: Use view(turn=1, continuous_seconds=4, native_audio=false, full_detail=true). At which film times did the displayed picture visibly change compared with the preceding displayed picture? Return only {"times":[...]} using seconds from the start. An unchanged picture gives an empty list.
